title: Applied ML Evals: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization, and Regression Playbook
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Overview

This playbook collects Redwood Inference's recommended end-to-end practices for model onboarding into the eval harness, authoring and maintaining prompt sets & benchmarks, applying quantization profiles safely, and triaging regressions. It is intended for ML engineers, applied researchers, and platform engineers responsible for bringing models into production.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-serving for new models while ensuring quality is preserved.
- Provide deterministic, reproducible evaluation steps to detect regressions early.
- Document clear thresholds, ownership, and runbooks for regression triage.
- Standardize quantization handoffs and safe rollout practices.

Scope
Covers the following sub-processes:
1) Eval harness onboarding checklist and standards
2) Prompt sets and benchmark creation & maintenance
3) Quantization profile development and validation
4) Regression detection, prioritization, and triage playbook
5) Continuous monitoring and rollout policies

Audience and ownership
- Primary audience: ML Engineers, Applied ML team, Model Onboarding owners.
- Owner_team: engineering.
- Secondary stakeholders: Product (feature owners), Eng SRE (observability), Security (if customer data used).

1) Eval harness onboarding checklist
Purpose: Ensure every candidate model is evaluated against consistent datasets, metrics, and compute profiles so we can compare models fairly and make rollout decisions.

Required artifacts before onboarding
- Model artifact (container or TFX package) with reproducible inference entrypoint and model metadata (arch, tokenizer, sequence limits).
- Model card including intended use, limitations, and safety considerations.
- Owner/Contact and SLA requirements (latency/cost expectations).
- Baseline prompt-set and evaluation config YAML (see example below).

Minimum evaluation suite (execute in CI + nightly runs)
- Functional correctness: task-specific test suites (e.g., summarization, Q&A).
- Safety checks: toxicity, PII leakage heuristics, instruction-following adversarial prompts.
- Performance metrics: tokens/sec, p99 latency on standard sequence lengths, memory footprint.
- Cost estimates: per-token cost projection for standard throughput.
- Regression tests: baseline performance vs current production model on canonical regression sets.

Onboarding steps (numbered)
1. Create model metadata file and register draft model entry in the eval harness registry.
2. Run smoke tests locally using the harness: unit prompts, tokenization checks, and API contract validation.
3. Execute full eval suite in CI (see job labels: eval/ci/model-onboard). Save artifacts and links to run logs.
4. Review results with the reviewer(s). Sign-off criteria: no failing safety checks, core task accuracy within threshold, latency within target band.
5. Schedule a canary rollout in dedicated staging pool and monitor for 48-72 hours.

Example evaluation config (YAML snippet)
| field | example |
|------|---------|
| model_name | my-model-v1 |
| tokenizer | huggingface/xyz |
| eval_sets | summarization-standard, qna-canonical, safety-basic |
| metrics | rouge-l, exact_match, toxicity-score |

2) Prompt sets and benchmark guidelines
Prompt-set hygiene and ownership
- Every prompt set must have an owner, a short description, and labels for domain, difficulty, and language.
- Use human-reviewed canonical answers where possible. If synthetic gold is used, label it as such.
- Version prompt sets using the harness (semantic versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) and store diffs in the prompt-sets repo.

Design principles
- Representative: include real-world inputs spanning short/long sequences, edge cases, and locale variations.
- Non-redundant: avoid duplicated prompts across benchmark splits.
- Challenge examples: include adversarial/instructional prompts to stress instruction-following and safety.

Benchmarking cadence and evaluation thresholds
- Run full benchmark on every model PR and weekly on production models.
- Alert if metric delta > configured thresholds (see thresholds table).
| metric | alert threshold | action |
| rouge-l | delta <= -3.0 pts | Triage: investigate prompt sensitivity |
| exact_match | delta <= -2.0 pts | Hold rollout, run targeted analyses |
| toxicity-score | increase >= +0.5 (scale dependent) | Immediate safety review |

3) Quantization profile process
Purpose: Reduce cost and memory without materially degrading quality.

Quantization stages
- Stage 0: Offline candidate selection and static analysis (layer sensitivity, activation ranges).
- Stage 1: Per-layer quantization experiments in the harness (FP16->INT8 simulated).
- Stage 2: Full-model quantized build validated with full eval suite and worst-case tests.
- Stage 3: Canary rollout using dedicated quantized pool with traffic shaping.

Acceptance criteria for a quantized profile
- Quality: end-to-end benchmark metrics within predefined drift windows (e.g., <= 1.5% relative drop in key metrics), no safety regressions.
- Performance: memory footprint reduced by target (example 2x for INT8), latency changes within accepted range.
- Stability: no increase in flakiness or OOM incidents in stress tests.

Example quantization checklist
1. Run automated sensitivity reports.
2. Generate candidate quantization configs (per-layer exceptions allowed).
3. Run full eval including adversarial prompts and long-context workloads.
4. If pass, create quantization profile PR with benchmarking artifacts and request reviewer sign-off.
5. Canary in staging for 72 hours with side-by-side traffic against baseline.

4) Regression triage playbook
This section defines detection, prioritization, and remediation steps for model regressions.

Detection signals (inputs to triage)
- Nightly/historical benchmark diffs crossing alert thresholds.
- Customer-reported regressions (support ticket with example).
- Monitoring alerts from production metrics: latency p95/p99 spike, error rate increases, or increased hallucination rate from quality probes.

Triage flow (high-level)
1. Acknowledge & assign: owner_team (model owner) must acknowledge within 4 hours for high-severity alerts.
2. Reproduce: run failing prompt(s) against current model and recent baseline in the eval harness. Capture raw outputs, tokens, and seeds.
3. Scope: determine whether regression is model, quantization, infra (kernel), or prompt/temperature change.
4. Prioritize: severity levels
   - Sev 1 (blocker): production-wide functional regression or safety violation -> rollback immediate.
   - Sev 2 (high): noticeable customer impact but limited scope -> pause rollout, mitigation options.
   - Sev 3 (medium): minor metric degradation -> schedule fix in next sprint.
5. Mitigate: options include temporary rollback to known-good model, adjust routing policies to fallback variant, or enable stricter prompting safeguards.
6. Root cause analysis and fix: open a task with RCA, owner, and ETA.
7. Postmortem: publish incident summary if Sev 1/2 with timeline, impact, and preventive actions.

Evidence to collect for RCA
- Eval harness run ids and artifacts.
- Model and quantization profile hashes.
- Inference logs (traces, kernel versions, hardware type).
- Prompt/temperature/seed metadata.

5) Monitoring, alerts, and rollout guidance
Key metrics and SLOs to monitor
- Quality SLOs (example): task-specific metric floors (rouge-l >= X, exact_match >= Y) measured daily.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 450ms on standard short sequence profile.
- Error budget: < 0.1% server errors over rolling 30d window for Dedicated customers.

Alerting thresholds (examples)
- Quality delta alert: any daily delta beyond configured threshold -> create triage ticket.
- Latency spike: p95 increase > 25% -> page oncall.
- Safety regression: any increase in high-severity toxicity flags -> immediate page to safety oncall.

Rollout pattern recommendations
- Canary: route 1-5% traffic to new model for 24-72 hours with metric comparison.
- Progressive ramp: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with automated checks between steps.
- Abort conditions: metric delta breach, customer complaints > threshold, critical errors.

Appendices
A. Standard command snippets
- Run harness locally: 
  ./harness/run_eval.sh --model my-model-v1 --config eval_configs/summarization.yaml --out artifacts/run-$(date +%F)
- Snapshot quantization report: 
  python tools/quant_report.py --model-hash abc123 --out reports/quant-abc123.json

B. Contact and escalation matrix
- Model owner: listed in model card (required).
- Applied ML lead: Daniel Park (pager for Sev 1 safety regressions).
- SRE oncall: see eng-sre oncall rota page.
